stages.a: The block at the pillowy stage, with a long shallow slit across the bag.
stages.v: Pull blocks at the pillowy stage and cut a long shallow slit or X, well into the block to scar the outer mat. Do not wait for pins.

stages.a: A white knob of tissue pushes out of the slit.
stages.v: Fruit at 13-18 °C, about 16 °C for HeCNS, with RH in the upper 80s to low 90s %.

stages.a: The knob rounds into a ball covered in short spines, all pointing down.
stages.v: Too high a humidity gives uneven spines; swings help them grow evenly. A wide CO2 swing gives "dreadlocks".

stages.a: A compact white pom-pom with short, even spines.
stages.v: Pick well before full maturity, on even spine growth: 14-20 days at about 16-17 °C.

stages.a: The spines grow long and droop, and spores fall.
stages.v: Late signs: long, drooping spines, dropping spores, fruit swelling with water. It should start and finish white.

labels.a: The long shallow slit in the bag.
labels.v: Cut too late and the fruit grows malformed inside the bag; too early raises contamination risk.

labels.a: A dense white ball of tissue.
labels.v: Pink or yellow tints on young fruit mostly mean the room is too dry.

labels.a: Short spines hang down all over the ball.
labels.v: The cue is even spine growth. HeCNS has short spines that do not droop.

labels.a: Dense and compact: the shape buyers want.
labels.v: A good HeCNS block carries several large, compact pom-poms.
Long, drooping spines that swell with water mean you are late.

labels.a: Spores fall from the spine tips.
labels.v: Dropping spores is a late sign.
